messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU host gpu-23 in cluster-prod-1 reporting sustained paging + kernel OOM warnings. Auto-runbook attached: <https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-paging|gpu-paging>. Severity: P1.

alex (oncall): Acked. Jumping in. Any obvious customer impact yet?

maria (sre): Seeing elevated 95th latency on /generate from 04:30 UTC, error spikes ~04:33. Support, can you confirm customer error reports?

jordan (support): Two customers reported timeouts and partial responses (chat sessions truncated). IDs: cust-8271, cust-9912. Estimated impact ~2.5% of requests last 20m. Logging convo snippets to the incident doc. :frowning:

sam (runtime): Dumping quick metrics from the runtime and nvidia:```
GPU 0: 24576 MiB total, used 23840 MiB, free 736 MiB
nvml: gpu mem fragmentation ratio ~0.86
runtime_kvcache: entries=1.2M hits=8.3M evictions=120k swap_events=860
batcher: inflight_batches=48 avg_batch_size=12 target_batch_size=32
recent_ooms=3 (kernel OOMs showing page faults while allocating KV pages)
```

lee (ml): That mem fragmentation ratio is nasty. Were we doing any quantized variant rollouts or large sequence length spikes?

sam (runtime): No rollout. Traces show a spike in long-context requests (avg seq len up to 4x baseline) around 04:29, correlated with large batches piling up. Batcher didn't backpressure fast enough.

alex (oncall): Immediate mitigations proposal: 1) reduce target_batch_size to 8 on canary pool; 2) enable aggressive kvcache eviction policy (evict_hot_lru=true) for canary; 3) route 10% traffic away from affected AZ. Canary first, 5m observe. Who will execute?

maria (sre): I can push batch config to canary in 2m. I'll also flip eviction flag. Will monitor mem and page-faults.

sam (runtime): Prepping CLI:```
# set canary batch size
redwoodctl set pool canary-gpu-23 --target-batch-size=8
# enable aggressive eviction
redwoodctl set runtime canary-gpu-23 --kvcache-evict-policy=hot-lru --kvcache-max-bytes=18000000000
```

alex (oncall): Execute and post results. Also capture dmesg if kernel OOM recurs.

(maria (sre) pasted): Done applied to canary at 04:36.

sam (runtime): Observing immediate drop in avg_batch_size -> 9 then 7. KV evictions spiked (extra 45k) and swap_events decreased. New snapshot:```
GPU 0: used 22410 MiB, free 2166 MiB
runtime_kvcache: entries=1.15M hits=8.4M evictions=165k swap_events=140
batcher: inflight_batches=22 avg_batch_size=9
page_fault_rate: down 70% vs peak
```

jordan (support): Early customer feedback: cust-9912 reports sessions recovered after ~2 minutes, cust-8271 still saw truncation but better. Marking customer impact as partial degradation resolved for most.

lee (ml): Hypotheses to track in RCA: A) sudden long-context tail causing oversized KV allocations + fragmentation; B) batcher backpressure slow -> transient spikes; C) a small memory leak in a recent runtime change that amplifies fragmentation under load.

alex (oncall): Owners: A -> lee, B -> sam, C -> maria investigate runtime memory accounting diffs against last deploy. Keep concise hypothesis updates in this thread.

maria (sre): Quick check: no new runtime binary deployed to that pool in last 24h. Accounting diff looks within noise but will run allocator snapshots.

sam (runtime): Running a replay on staging with long-context traffic and the old batch config to reproduce. If reproduced, we flip the batching backpressure algorithm (reduce batch_window_ms) as a second mitigation.

lee (ml): I'll pull the prompt distribution and check for a customer or job that might be generating repeated long contexts. Also will check model kv page size patterns.

alex (oncall): If canary stays stable for 10m, we'll roll the batch/evict changes to 30% then 100% with watch. If we see kernel OOM again we'll escalate to host replacement.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=P1 -> partial mitigation in progress. Playbook link: <https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-paging#mitigations>.

jordan (support): Noting both customers for post-incident comms. Creating follow-up ticket to verify data retention and truncated output remediation.

maria (sre): Leaving detailed logs and dmesg extract in the incident doc. If anyone needs raw dumps I can share s3 links. Handoff: I'll be on-call for the next 40m; if unsteady at handoff time, I'll escalate to infra lead.

alex (oncall): Thanks all. I'm going to update the incident timeline and start the RCA doc skeleton. Add timeline entries as you see fit. Handoff to next oncall in ~35m unless we need continued support. :thumbsup:
